featured_reviews.name: Shriraj Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing for a Place Known for Biryani

I visited this restaurant with high expectations because it’s known for its biryani, but unfortunately the experience was a big letdown.

We ordered:
Malai Tikka
Lollipop Masala
Large Chicken Dum Biryani

The Lollipop Masala was the only item that stood out. It was flavorful, almost like a Schezwan-style lollipop, and honestly the best part of the entire meal.

The Malai Tikka, however, was very disappointing. The chicken was rubbery, didn’t taste fresh, and despite decent presentation, the flavor and texture were not enjoyable at all.

Now coming to the main attraction - the Large Chicken Dum Biryani (around ₹600). For this price, getting only 3 pieces of chicken already felt underwhelming. The rice lacked the rich aroma and layered spices that you expect from a good dum biryani. There was barely any biryani masala, and while the chicken was technically well-cooked in dum style, it had very little flavor.

Overall, the biryani felt plain, dull, and nowhere close to what a place with “Biryani” in its name should serve.

What made it even more disappointing was that friends who had visited earlier said the food used to be much better - but this time none of us enjoyed it.

Final verdict:
For a restaurant called Biryani Darbar, the biryani does not live up to the name at all. I’m giving 2 stars only because of the Lollipop Masala. Everything else was far below expectations.

I really hope they improve the consistency and quality because right now, it does not justify the price or reputation.

Feedback noted. It would have been more helpful if you have informed Captain about the same and we would have checked and addressed this immediately. We truly believe in customer service. Also, there were no such complaints from any of our customers. We apologise for your experience and hope you allow us another chance to serve you better. Thank you.

featured_reviews.name: Suketu CHANDAN
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Biryani Darbar and it was an absolute delight!

Biryani here is easily one of the best I've had in Mumbai. Perfectly cooked long-grain rice, perfect vegetable masala and that rich, fragrant dum-cooked flavor with just the right balance of spicey, not too oily, not too dry, just perfect. The raita and salan that came with it were excellent accompaniments.

For desserts, I tried both Gajar Halwa and Shahi Tukda, and both were outstanding!
The Gajar Halwa was rich, moist, and packed with the natural sweetness of carrots, loaded with ghee, nuts, and khoya. It tasted completely homemade – warm, comforting, and indulgent.

Shahi Tukda was equally impressive – crispy fried bread soaked in fragrant saffron milk, topped with nuts and a touch of rose water. It had the perfect texture contrast and wasn't overly sweet. Both desserts felt luxurious and authentic.
The service was quick and friendly, and the portions were generous. Ambiance is simple but comfortable – perfect for a hearty meal with family or friends.

If you're a biryani lover or craving proper Mughlai desserts, Biryani Darbar Goregaon is a must-visit. Everything we ordered was top-notch. Easily one of the best biryani places in the area.

Highly recommended – 5 Stars! 🔥
Will definitely be going back soon.

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. Unfortunately, the Prawns Chilly starter was a letdown, featuring tiny, chewy prawns and an average sauce that we ultimately couldn't finish.
However, the highly anticipated Chicken Biryani completely redeemed the meal. It was absolutely perfect, boasting a flawless blend of spices, tender meat, and a delicious accompanying raita that made the whole visit worthwhile. We wrapped up with the Apricot Delight dessert, which was spectacularly flavorful and highly recommended.
Across the board, the portions were much larger than expected, justifying the slightly expensive pricing, and the service from the super nice staff was excellent. My only critique is that they should expand their soft drink menu beyond standard Pepsi and Coca-Cola to include options like Campa, Big Cola, and Lahori to better complement their heavy, flavorful dishes.

We ordered the half Murg Mussallam, which came with two rich and flavorful gravies – one a vibrant yellow and the other a deep red. The dish was generously topped with juicy tandoori chicken pieces, making it both unique and hearty. Paired with butter garlic naan, the meal was absolutely satisfying and more than enough for two people.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian pudding, which was a real highlight – rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced in flavor. The caramel custard was just as expected – smooth and classic, a comforting end to the meal.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A special shoutout to the kitchen for the thoughtful preparation and presentation.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for flavorful Non veg Indian dishes and comforting desserts in a relaxed setting.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.

Their special thali, butter chicken, dal tadka, and tandoori items are highly recommended and must-try dishes.
Cleanliness and hygiene are the biggest strengths of Raj Restaurant. From floors, tables, and chairs to everything is maintained spotlessly clean. Great care is taken in food preparation, making it a safe and hygienic place to dine.
The staff is polite, quick, and very cooperative. From taking orders to serving food, everything is done in a professional and friendly manner. Their smiling service makes the overall experience even more pleasant.
If you are looking for great taste, cleanliness, and excellent service in Goregaon, Raj Restaurant is the perfect choice. I strongly recommend it and happily give it a 5-star rating.

Just had the most nostalgic breakfast experience at Raj Restaurant after a decade! I used to frequent this place back in 2009, and their kheema pav was always my go-to dish. Even back then, it was a popular spot among Patkar College students, and for good reason - the kheema pav is truly timeless.

Fast forward to October 2025, and I'm thrilled to report that the taste remains unchanged. The same recipe, the same flavors, the same love. It brought back a flood of memories, and I couldn't help but tear up. The AC section is a new addition since my time, but some things remain the same - their commitment to serving delicious food that hits the spot every time.

If you're a kheema pav lover like me, do try it out. It's a classic dish that stands the test of time. Raj Restaurant has been through its ups and downs, but one thing that's constant is their amazing kheema fry pav. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nita Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Woke up craving for idli and dosa and we've practically eaten from every south indian restaurant in Goregaon so wanted to try a place that claimed it gave a home style experience. Since we're south indians too, we expected it to taste exactly how they promised it to. The super soft idli and the set dosai immediately transported us to Mangalore. Absolutely loved the fact that it's not trying to please anybody and give people an authentic experience. The sambar and chutney were exactly what is made at home.

The packaging was refreshingly good. The dosa came in a pizza type box which kept the shape intact and the idlis were in a nice plate box. Loved everything about this.

The manager was sweet enough to call up and tell us the taste we'd expect from the sambar would be different from what we're used to eating but tbh, that's exactly what we wanted.

I think I've found a permanent breakfast place in Mumbai! Can't wait for them to start making vadas too. 100% recommend this place if you want a authentic experience. You'll find the mainstream kinds everywhere, this was uniquely "homely". Love it!

featured_reviews.name: Jayant Wankhede
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lalit Fine Dine is such a Wonderful place for dine. This is suitable for both Vegetarians as well as Non Vegetarian person. The ambience is a classic wonderful. This is not only a type of Casual Family restaurant but also there you can dine with your besties or family.

The Food was awesome in taste. There I had tried 5-6 dishes and every items that I had tried was superb. I haved tried Non veg food it was also really delicious. The taste of the food is so yummy and it never forgetable.

What we tried :-

Starter :-

• Chicken Tandoori - Firstly we ordered starter & it was amazing. Tandoori was nicely cooked and juicy & especially you get some salad with Tandoori.

Main Course :-

• Murg Masulam - Murg Masulam was the dish which impressed me alot. Chicken was not boneless but the quantity and quality of food is amazing. The taste of masulam is little spicy and nice. Spicy lover will go through this dish. *Highly recommended*

• Chicken Amritsari - The dish comes with boneless chicken. The Chicken pieces were extremely soft & tasty, chicken was little tangy & spicy in taste. You can try this with butter roti. Again *Highly recommended*

Mocktails :-

• Strawberry Delight - Mocktail was quite good which i felt. It comes with little sweet and taste of strawberry. It's mixture of orange juice, pineapple juice & strawberry juice crush.

• Virgin Pinacaloda - This Mocktail comes under Funky Coolers. It's Lychee and vanilla ice cream shaken to make a perfect mocktail.

• Intimate Joy - This one is my favorite. It's mixture of lemon juice, khus syrup, 7 up toop with sabja. I really like this Mocktail. And i will recommend to other's also.

Dessert :-

• Sizzling Brownie - The piece of soft cake, chocolate syrup and vanilla ice cream all are perfect & it's perfect way to end our meal.

I am giving four star because we need to wait for longer time per order. Otherwise the quality of food is good.

Ratna Veg Restaurant in Goregaon West has become one of our regular breakfast spots after weekend gym workouts. It's a simple and reliable place to enjoy a satisfying South Indian breakfast without burning a hole in your pocket.

On my recent visit, I tried their Cheese Masala Dosa, and it was absolutely delicious. The dosa was crisp, generously filled, and had just the right amount of cheese without overpowering the traditional flavors. Definitely a must-try if you're visiting for breakfast.

Apart from South Indian dishes, they also offer a good variety of North Indian food, making it a convenient option for different cravings throughout the day. The service is usually quick, and the food is served fresh and hot.

The ambience is fairly average and nothing particularly fancy, but the quality of food makes up for it. If you're looking for a dependable place for a tasty breakfast or a casual meal with family and friends, Ratna Veg Restaurant is worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Sanntosh Shringarpure
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hits and misses at this Mangalorean spot:

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

featured_reviews.name: Kamlesh Gadilohar
featured_reviews.review_text:
1/5 – One of the Worst Mughlai Dining Experiences We've Had

We visited Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West for my brother's birthday celebration, expecting the quality and hospitality associated with the Delhi Darbar name. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the most disappointing dining experiences we've had.

We started with roasted and fried papad. The roasted papad had a small hair on it. I quietly removed it without informing my family to avoid spoiling the occasion, but such hygiene lapses should never happen.

For starters, we ordered the Shahi Kebab Platter, Mutton Kebab, and Finger Chips. The kebabs were the only items that tasted genuinely good, although the quantity was quite small. Even the Finger Chips portion was surprisingly small considering the pricing.

The rest of the food was disappointing:

Veg Crispy was overloaded with oil and had the smell of reused cooking oil. We hardly ate any of it and packed almost the entire dish. Nobody from the staff bothered to ask whether there was an issue.
Chicken Schezwan Tandoori seemed to be prepared using stale tandoori chicken.
Butter Chicken was very average and lacked the richness expected from a reputed Mughlai restaurant.
Mutton Masala was swimming in oil and had an ordinary taste.
Paneer Tikka Biryani contained hard paneer pieces, excessive oil, and very little flavor.
The Chicken Dum Biryani was the biggest disappointment. The rice quality was shockingly poor, consisting largely of broken "tukda" rice that we wouldn't even use for khichdi at home. It was excessively oily and filled with potato pieces. For a restaurant known for Mughlai cuisine, serving a biryani of this quality is simply unacceptable.

The service was equally disappointing. At one point, one of our family members had to get a plate himself because the attending manager was busy on a phone call. The manager came across as rude, inattentive, and unprofessional. Basic hospitality and customer service seemed completely missing.

What made the experience even more frustrating was that despite several dishes being left unfinished, no one from the staff showed any concern or made an effort to understand whether there was a problem with the food.

Our bill exceeded ₹5,000, yet the overall quality of food and service was nowhere near the level expected for that price. My family and I have dined at numerous Mughlai restaurants across Mumbai over the years, ranging from small establishments to premium dining venues, and this was honestly one of the worst experiences we've had.

A birthday celebration that should have been memorable for the right reasons ended up being memorable for all the wrong ones.

Poor food quality, excessive use of oil, questionable freshness, hygiene concerns, small portions, indifferent service, and premium pricing that simply doesn't match the experience. Based on this visit, I would not recommend Delhi Darbar, Jogeshwari West.

It’s disheartening to learn about your recent visit and the shortcomings you experienced. The hygiene issue with the papad is particularly concerning, and I sincerely apologize for this lapse. We take cleanliness seriously and will investigate how this occurred. 
Thanks & Regards,
Jaffer Bhais Delhi Darbar

featured_reviews.review_text:
Important Notice to All Customers:
It’s a humble request to please avoid placing any orders from Lazeez Caterers, Goregaon (Mr. Haroon Khan – Owner) for any occasion.

I have been one of their regular customers for over 10 years, and it’s truly disappointing that I have to write this as a concerned and loyal consumer, but I don’t want anyone else to face the same experience.

We had ordered 1.5 kg Chicken Tikka Biryani and 24 Seekh Rolls for our family members on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. Unfortunately, the biryani contained mostly rice with very few chicken pieces and dry masala, even after specifically informing the caterer in advance that we wanted it flavorful and not dry. The seekh rolls were also extremely salty and unpalatable.

We returned 1 kg of biryani and the seekh rolls and shared our feedback, yet the owner showed no courtesy, offered no discount or replacement, and instead insisted on full payment including delivery charges, without taking any responsibility for the poor quality.

I was genuinely disappointed with the food quality, the service, and the arrogant attitude of the owner over the phone. Despite everything, I still paid the full amount of ₹2400 via GPay.

Kindly take note before placing any orders from this vendor. 🙏🏻

Overall pathetic service, unacceptable and really disappointed.

featured_reviews.name: Gulshan Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have explored almost every food joint in Mumbai, but ever since I discovered Biryani by Story, I have stopped looking elsewhere. I’ve been ordering from here continuously, and for a good reason—it tastes exactly like 'Maa ke haath ka khana' (mother’s handmade food).

While their name says Biryani, their entire menu is a masterpiece of home-style cooking. Their Chicken Curry is rich and flavorful without being greasy, and when paired with their soft Rotis, it’s pure comfort. I also highly recommend their Aloo Bhujiya and Mix Vegetables—they have that authentic, simple, and soul-satisfying taste that is so hard to find in a big city.

If you are tired of oily restaurant food and crave a meal that feels like home, Biryani by Story is the place to order from. It’s not just food; it’s an emotion!"
